title: 233. Algebra, Equations & Inequalities: Work-Rate Problems with Rational Equations
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.concept: Work rate as a reciprocal of time
questions.learningObjective: Determine the work rate from the time required to complete a job.
questions.question: A worker can complete a job in \(6\) hours. What is the worker's rate in jobs per hour?
questions.explanation:
Work rate is the amount of work completed per unit of time. If the worker completes \(1\) job in \(6\) hours, then the rate is
\[
\frac{1\text{ job}}{6\text{ hours}}=\frac{1}{6}\text{ job per hour}
\]
Therefore the correct rate is \(\frac{1}{6}\).

questions.concept: Combined work rate for two pipes
questions.learningObjective: Form an equation for the combined rate of two pipes filling a tank.
questions.question: Pipe A fills a tank in \(4\) hours, and pipe B fills the same tank in \(6\) hours. If both pipes are opened together, the tank is filled in \(t\) hours. Which equation represents this situation?
questions.explanation:
Pipe A fills \(\frac{1}{4}\) of the tank per hour, and pipe B fills \(\frac{1}{6}\) of the tank per hour. Together they fill
\[
\frac{1}{4}+\frac{1}{6}
\]
of the tank per hour. Since the whole tank is filled in \(t\) hours, their combined rate is also \(\frac{1}{t}\). Therefore the equation is
\[
\frac{1}{t}=\frac{1}{4}+\frac{1}{6}
\]
questions.hint: The combined rate is the sum of the individual rates.

questions.concept: Combined work rate for two workers
questions.learningObjective: Form an equation for the combined work rate of two workers.
questions.question: Worker A can complete a job in \(10\) hours, and worker B can complete the same job in \(15\) hours. If they work together, the job is completed in \(t\) hours. Which equation represents this situation?
questions.explanation:
Worker A's rate is \(\frac{1}{10}\) job per hour, and worker B's rate is \(\frac{1}{15}\) job per hour. Together their rate is
\[
\frac{1}{10}+\frac{1}{15}
\]
Since they complete the job in \(t\) hours, their combined rate is also \(\frac{1}{t}\). Therefore the equation is
\[
\frac{1}{10}+\frac{1}{15}=\frac{1}{t}
\]
questions.hint: Add the individual rates to obtain the combined rate.

questions.learningObjective: Form a rational equation when one worker takes longer than another.
questions.question: Worker A can complete a job in \(x\) hours, and worker B takes \(3\) hours longer than worker A. Together they complete the job in \(2\) hours. Which equation represents this situation?
questions.explanation:
Worker A's rate is \(\frac{1}{x}\), and worker B's rate is \(\frac{1}{x+3}\). Their combined rate is
\[
\frac{1}{x}+\frac{1}{x+3}
\]
Since they finish the job in \(2\) hours, their combined rate is \(\frac{1}{2}\). Therefore the equation is
\[
\frac{1}{x}+\frac{1}{x+3}=\frac{1}{2}
\]
questions.hint: Express each worker's rate as the reciprocal of that worker's time.

questions.learningObjective: Determine the time required for two pipes to fill a tank together.
questions.question: One pipe fills a tank in \(5\) hours, and another pipe fills the same tank in \(20\) hours. How long will it take both pipes to fill the tank together?
questions.explanation:
The first pipe fills \(\frac{1}{5}\) of the tank per hour, and the second fills \(\frac{1}{20}\) of the tank per hour. Their combined rate is
\[
\frac{1}{5}+\frac{1}{20}=\frac{4}{20}+\frac{1}{20}=\frac{5}{20}=\frac{1}{4}
\]
Thus they fill \(\frac{1}{4}\) of the tank per hour, so the whole tank is filled in \(4\) hours.
questions.hint: Add the rates, then take the reciprocal of the combined rate to find the total time.

questions.concept: Work-rate problem with one worker leaving
questions.learningObjective: Determine the remaining time when one worker leaves after working together.
questions.question: Worker A can complete a job in \(8\) days, and worker B can complete it in \(12\) days. They work together for \(2\) days, and then A leaves. How many more days does B need to finish the remaining job alone?
questions.hint: Find the work completed in the first \(2\) days, then divide the remaining work by B's rate.

questions.concept: Solving for an unknown individual work time
questions.learningObjective: Determine one worker's time when the combined time and the other worker's time are known.
questions.question: A and B together can complete a job in \(6\) days. A alone can complete the job in \(10\) days. How long would B alone take to complete the job?
questions.hint: Use the combined-rate equation and solve for the unknown reciprocal time.

questions.concept: Solving for an unknown tap time
questions.learningObjective: Determine the time required for one tap to fill a tank alone.
questions.question: Two taps together fill a tank in \(12\) minutes. One tap alone fills the tank in \(20\) minutes. How long would the other tap take to fill the tank alone?
questions.hint: Set up the combined-rate equation and solve for the unknown time.

questions.learningObjective: Determine one worker's time from three pairwise combined work times.
questions.question: A and B together can complete a job in \(12\) days, B and C together in \(15\) days, and A and C together in \(20\) days. How long would A alone take to complete the job?
questions.hint: Add the three pairwise rate equations, then subtract the pair that does not include A.

questions.concept: Work-rate problem with a delayed start
questions.learningObjective: Determine the total time when one worker starts later.
questions.question: Worker A can complete a job in \(10\) hours, and worker B can complete it in \(15\) hours. A works alone for \(3\) hours, and then B joins A. How long does it take to complete the job from the moment A starts?
questions.hint: Find the work completed by A alone, then divide the remaining work by the combined rate.
